unresolved.text: Allocator-derived values (base block, TBW, packed descriptor, available count, cursors, occupancy) are NOT read from the ELF; the "model" fields come from a replay of the native Ps2TextureMemory and are not independent source evidence. They must be reproduced by the unchanged original 0x1cf008 before use.

Indirect calls (jalr) inside the call closures are counted but not resolved. Address-taken functions that reach a resource root exist (data pointers: 0x18f7a8 at 0x1fe308; scene/jump-table entries) but no startup call site was shown to dispatch to them other than 0x18f7a8 via 0x186aa8 (not in the prefix).

Handle ids and record indices (0..35) assume first-fit HR allocation and FIFO record list with no reservation (0x1cd5c8 is not reachable) and no earlier handle creation; derived by reading, not observed.

GS-register-level behaviour of the SDK/system init calls (0x1c7730, 0x1c6918, 0x16c1e0, 0x1c8b40, 0x1cff30, 0x1cb1c0) is not decoded; their closures reach DMA/GS helper functions (0x1e1750, 0x1e1840, 0x1e5f48, 0x1e48a0). No VRAM allocator, handle, upload or draw-list root is reachable, but a GS reset or clear writing VRAM contents is not excluded by this static pass.
VU1 microprogram uploads (0x1ace90, 0x1b1e60, 0x1795e8) are classified as VIF MPG packets from the packet structure (0x1afa40) and call shape; the packet bytes were not decoded exhaustively.

Effect system init inside 0x103a88 (0x1143d8, 0x10bc78: 103d30/103b78/1138c0/113f00/114058/10ba38) was not read instruction by instruction; no resource root is reachable but GS register/packet writes are not excluded.
Allocator slots 0x213574/0x213578/0x21357c/0x213580 are installed at runtime; 0x21357c is read as a trim/realloc (hypothesis). Host-heap behaviour is irrelevant to VRAM but not resolved.

The noise texture and both noise CLUTs depend on the libc rand() state. The seed word (1) comes from the ELF .data image and no srand call site is reachable, and 0x192ea0 is the first rand consumer by static closure; a hidden earlier rand() call through a jalr is not excluded. The Python replay is derived from reading, not compared with an original run.

Filter CLUT 1/2 (0x332a68, 0x332a78) bytes: no write inside the prefix was found (0x1902d8 is reached only through the 0x2003c8 callback table from the filter dispatcher 0x18f9f8, which runs after the first scheduler traversal at 0x100628). Colour/depth/capture buffer bytes: no draw, clear or copy that executes inside the prefix was found; the two recorded display lists (0x332a70, 0x332a84) are not kicked.
Exact host-to-local packet chunking and the GS state left by uploads (0x1cba48/0x1c9bb8) were read for argument flow only; PSM20/36/44 qwc = w*h>>5 is from the 0x1c9b48 jump table.
Failure paths (allocation failure, load failure) were not exercised; the executed contract assumes success, which the native model confirms for the allocator (no failed allocation in the replay).
Whether 0x1ed1c0, 0x16c1e0 (and similar leaf/library calls) have effects on texture memory is argued only by absence of roots in the jal closure.
